title: For a pocket notebook, go with the classic!
text:

There are cheaper options. But the Field Notes brand paper, binding, and covers are tried and true. There are also more expensive options...but for a notebook you’re just going to shove into a pocket, how much do you really want to spend?

I got lots of extra erasers in both sizes, so I should not run out any time soon. I like to shave the end to a pencil point to erase finer areas. It is definitely worth keeping in my coloring kit.

I filled the cartridge with Diamine Aurora Borealis ink and it writes very well. Another Lamy pen to add to my growing collection.

They stand up to cabin pressure when I fly, very important as I am a frequent flier. Sheening and shimmering inks can be used in these for caligraphy. Very nice!

title: Gorgeous color!

Another great addition to my Lamy collection!

title: Perfectly Named Ink
text: Sublime, sumptuous color!  I confess that I love the warm colored inks (anything from gold to dark red), but this is like a series of different colors in one bottle!  I have rarely seen an ink that behaves to give a range of colors with a generously flowing fountain pen.  A thin bit of ink gives a beautiful golden yellow, and heavier amounts go to a rich golden orange.  I have to say that whoever named it, got it exactly right:  it does look like a western sunset sky.  Wonderful rich color!

title: Excellent Pen for Customization
text: The pen is really nice, solid, good quality.  I love being able to see the ink level, and to change the nib if I want to. The happy ending to the story is that I ordered a different nib (a 1.1 stub), and the pen works exactly the way I had wanted.  The nib was easy to replace, and although there's a small added expense of a new nib, I still am very happy with the pen.

title: Too Light To Read

This pen writes surprisingly well. I bought it on a whim because of the price, and fully expected it to be garbage. The pen has weight to it, which I like. I inked it with some Diamine Ancient Copper and was shocked at how smooth it wrote. It writes better than my $25 Lamy Safari.

Took a while to get here, but I wasn't in a hurry. If you're in the market for a fountain pen, and you don't want to spend more than a few dollars, I would highly recommend this one, especially if you're ju

title: Excellent fountain pen for the price
text: I bought this on a whim because it was so inexpensive. I have to say, it's a great little fountain pen. I had low expectations because of the price, and I was pleasantly surprised. It writes better than I thought it would. It's not "scratchy" and lays down ink evenly. I use it quite a bit.

title: Nice ink. Bright blue color.
text: The ink, as with the all the Noodler's Inks I've used, is great. Not too fond of the color. It's not a dark blue. More of a "bright blue". Turns out that my daughter likes it much better than I do. Works great in her Lamy Safari with medium nib.

title: Nice ink. Beautiful color.
text: Love the color. It's a very dark red. Works well in my Monteverde Intima. Goes on a little wet, but dries quickly enough. Doesn't dry out in the pen. Have left it sitting for a couple of weeks without writing, and when I pick up my pen the ink flows just fine.

title: Perfect companion for Lamy Safari
text: I switched out the pre-filled ink cartridges in my Lamy Safari Fountain Pen (fine nib) with this converter. Works perfectly, and has allowed me to try several different inks. Well worth it if you want to experiment.

title: Diameter tolerance is poor
text: My lead holder can’t hold onto the 2B lead - it’s not thick enough lead. The 4B is way too soft to be usable - it’s nicely dark but has zero point retention.

title: Really light, good point retention
text: Lead is way too light for me, but the point retention is phenomenal. Feels like a 4H to me, to be honest.

title: Good highlighter ink.
text: Really nice green highlighter ink. I have been using it in a Lamy Al-Star with 1.9mm stub nib via a converter, and I have had no issues with corrosion or clogging. Flow is good, though a bit wet, and some pooling does occur. I don’t get much bleedthrough from a single pass on office copy paper, and there’s no feathering. I don’t use it to highlight over fountain pen ink, because that will s,ear or dissolve.

title: Good stub nib
text: Nice nib. Picture is not of the product. You are getting a 1.9mm stub. It’s smooth and well tuned. Awesome for calligraphy.

title: Awesome permanent ink
text:
I ordered Salix, which is a beautiful new-fashioned iron gall blue black ink. It is waterproof, and it changes from blue to a blue-black color, but it doesn’t hurt your pen, really. I left it in a converter pen for 2 months without cleaning with no issue. Love this ink.

The ink doesn’t bleed or feather for me, even on cheaper paper.

title: Good ink, not quite the right color.
text:
I ordered Verdigris, which I expected to be Verdi mixed with Gris - green and gray. This actually is more of a dark teal - decidedly more blue-black with a bit of green. I still like the color alright.

The ink behaves beautifully - wet, good flow, but no bleed or feathering even on field notes paper.

title: Excessively wet ink that behaves well
text: This ink is really wet. It shades a ton, and the flow is insanely smooth. The color is a deep teal color, and pairs well with my Lamy Safari Petrol. It’s dark enough that it can be used in professional settings, but it’s not a stuffy blue by any means. This ink does not bleed or feather on cheap paper, and it cleans really easily. Only knock is that it’s not water resistant.

title: A nice green
text: This is really a pretty great green. It’s got really good color, is easy to clean out of pens, has a little bit of water resistance, and shades subtly. The ink flows well, though is not excessively wet. It does have a tendency to bleed a bit on cheaper paper, and it also will look quite wooly on cheap paper. The bottle design is not great - the neck is rather slender, and the whole thing is not very deep. This makes filling directly from the bottle difficult as you use up the first half of it. Y

title: A nice black ink
text: This is a nice black ink. It has good flow, good color, and is not very prone to bleeding or feathering, even on cheap paper. The one thing that I don’t like is it tends to shade a little - something I don’t like in my blacks. It’s a huge quantity of ink for an affordable price.

title: It’s a pack of converters
text: It’s a pack of converters meant for the Lamy Safari, Lamy Vista, and Lamy Al-Star. They work fine and clean easily enough. I really wish that the piston knob was clear or black instead of red - it’s positively gaudy in my Lamy Vista. But at least I’m not stuck using Lamy cartridges...

title: Severely blue-green
text: I do not like this ink. This is advertised as a green ink, but it’s *really* blue-green. It’s not a color that I like at all. The ink has little to no water resistance, which is unfortunate. The flow tends on the dry side, which I don’t like. At least feathering and bleedthrough are not an issue with an EF nib, even on cheap paper.

title: A fine corrections ink
text: This is a standard red ink - nothing to write home about. The color is fine, though a bit too pink or unsaturated for my taste. It works fine as a corrections red ink, but not for writing. There is basically no water resistance to this ink. The flow is fine. There is little to no bleedthrough, showthrough, or feathering, even on cheap paper with this ink, which is nice.

title: Absurd pen, in the best possible way.
text: This pen is absolely ridiculous, in the best possible way. It’s really thick, and it’s really heavy, and I love it. The pen is made entirely of brass, and then painted. It looks super high quality, and it feels super high quality. It writes smoothly with a western medium sized nib. The nib looks incredible. Between this and the pilot vanishing point, I'm going with the e95s svery time.

I love the EF for everyday writing on bad paper, it's insanely smooth and nice and medium flowing. You're not gonna see much shading or sheen, but this was never the pen for that.

text:

I wish the nib had more scrollwork on it, it wouldn't be expensive to stamp on a flour

text:

It came with two ink cartridges but no converter (as is standard for all japanese pens short of the pilot metropolitan)

Pen feels good in the hand poste

title: Disappointing paper lets this otherwise great book down
text:
Great in most ways. I love the feel and color of the paper, the size is right, and the cover and stitching is extremely nice. But if you use fountain pens, it's rather mediocre. The overall paper coating quality is a little worse than Rhodia, towards the bottom of almost every page, the coating gets spotty and you get MASSIVE feathering at the pooling part of each pen stroke, even fine, fairly dry nibs struggle.

And to top it off, the Showthrough is borderline bleed. Noodlers golden b

text:
This is a spectacular budget notebook for fountain pen users. It's big, rough, overbuilt, and sturdy. Yes, you have to buy a 2 pack or 6 pack for the value to be there (a single notebook is NOT worth it at $8, but two for 10 or 6 for 22 is a GREAT deal)

text:
An incredible writer, beautiful design, solid materials, lovely nibs, great customer service, but the matte finish is a complete achilles' heel. it takes less than a week of normal use to start chipping the finish on the grip and anywhere else there's matte paint.

So what was a gorgeous pen that feels incredibly balanced, the cap posts well, and would otherwise be just outstanding, becomes a badly made piece of junk. Avoid the matte finish. I sent mine back to Yafa (who had excellent

text:
Not a fountain pen for beginners, noodlers pens require a thorough cleaning when you get them and often require a heat set too (dip the nib and feed in boiling water for 15 seconds, remove, then press the feed up against the nib for another 30 seconds with a paper towel to set the ebonite feed)

But properly heat set, these pens are great writers. The nibs are fine-medium (closer to a western fine but very wet so overall a fine-med) and they do actually flex. You can get a good 1.5mm l

title: So close to perfect it doesn't matter.
text:
About as close to perfect as pencils get.

Lead hardness indicator is on the back and has everything but 4B (which I have tried and is a stupid idea unless you like lead that snaps if you look at it funny and only writes one sentence before needing another click)

Clip is removable but quite tight.

Grip is absolutely the best. no amount of sweaty, gross hands will phase this thing's grip, it's like 60 grit sandpaper. And it can be washed if your hands are that gros

text:
For the price, this is probably one of the best mechanical pencils made. I still like the rotring 600/800 more due to the grip, but this is a great pencil.

First, the cons:
Firstly, it has a gimmicky little thing where you can twist the grip to make it "hard" or "soft". This is completely meaningless, since you have to press the pencil directly down on the page to make the spring engage, and it's so firm that it cuts the paper or snaps the lead. I kind of dislike

title: Clever idea, excellent execution, one of the best brands in writing instruments.
text:
A pencil with a cap. Who'd have thought? And the cap is a sharpener?

This is a freaking awesome idea. Faber Castell just makes such awesome products. I don't love their mechanical pencil (I just find the grip a bit slippery compared to rotring), but this thing is just the bee's knees. The sharpener is awesome, the cap keeps the point of your pencil safe, and the pencil it comes with is just spectacular (though it is a little short for some reason)

Overall if you're super pi

text:
Shipped quick, no issues with seller. I just don't think 4B lead makes any sense in a mechanical pencil unless you have a VERY specific use for it. If you want dark and saturated, maybe 2B is better.

This lead wears down hysterically fast. I thought 4b pencils wore down quickly but this is actually funny how fast it wears. As a result, you never have a sharp point, it instantly mushes down into what you'd call a medium or broad fountain pen line. Sketching with a very light hand is ok

title: Decent, but not great.
text:
Violet is a solid color. The bottle is decent (the cap has to be tightened kind of uncomfortably to make it line up with the body, the mouth opening is fairly sized, and it's not too squat, but it just doesn't look that spectacular somehow) but as someone who likes to keep their bottles in the packaging, this ink comes in a really bizarre floating plastic box that doesn't protect the ink from light, so it might fade over the years.

text:
This is the king of all ballpoints. As a fountain pen fanatic, I admit that sometimes they just don't work, particularly when you're forced to write in a terrible chemistry copybook that bleeds and feathers every ink known to man.

I bought this because I needed a ballpoint and the history of this pen is just fascinating. It's still made in the USA, on the same machines, with ZERO changes, as the original ones that went into space. I dig that. The ballpoints are spectacular with one ex

text:
These German sellers of Edelstein are lifesavers. Pelkikan Edelstein ink is spectacular, but insultingly overpriced in America. For $30, this ink is forgettable. For under $20, this stuff is a rocking deal. The bottles are awesome (not the most practical, but far from the worst, and they look amazing on any desk, with jewel like glass and a beautiful cap) And the ink is just stellar.

Medium flowing, medium-high saturation, some red sheen (reviewing Topaz) decent manners on bad paper,

title: Really awesome ink.
text:
One of the coolest inks out there, these R&K iron galls are very well mannered and a great deal.

Good shading, does down a very slate blue and darkens over the course of about 30 seconds to a real blue-black and over a day or two to a very dark blue black (never quite black like diamine registrar's)

It's not a super high ferro-gallic iron gall, meaning that it won't eat your fountain pen seals or steel nib. Similarly, it's not quite as amazing as platinum classic inks or Di

title: A very rare color indeed.
text:
True sepia color. Mild to no shading, no sheen, decent performance on bad paper, it's above average in all regards (decent waterproofness) but the color is very unique, and nobody else seems to make a really true sepia color. This ink looks weird on super white paper, but on cream or browned paper, this stuff looks absolutely incredible.

Shipping was extremely quick, this is my fourth R&K ink, and not one of them has disappointed.

title: Fantastic notebook, but not great for people who use it for taking classroom notes
text:
I bought this in a stationary shop not knowing the back of each page is blank. Which is a bummer. Because this paper blows rhodia/clairefontaine out of the freaking water, and even the meanest ink in the wettest fountain pen nib doesn't bleed or show through.

This pen is the same delike brass pen that has been gaining notoriety lately in the fountain pen community.

text:
Lamy nibs are just not that exceptional. I don't get the hype. The one thing they do well is swap easily, so the CP-1 I use for all my ink reviews, I can simply swap all the nibs out on the same pen and have an EF, F, M, B, and 1.1 in the sample with only having to clean and fill one pen.

I don't like M nibs anyways, this is a fairly wet M, it's not glassy smooth or perfectly tuned feedback like the Faber Castell Loom, it's a very basic, slightly toothy, a hair scratchy.

text:
Kind of... Meh. It's not the warm autum grey I was hoping, much colder. It's not steel grey like Sailor Chu Shu, but it's a very flat grey. It reminds me of the "Before" filter placed on an antidepressant commercial.

text:

text:
I really prefer the con50 to this. The 50 has a heavier agitator, which did "click" a little more, but it also was able to mix up shimmering inks, and the beads in this simply aren't heavy enough to break the tension on the more viscous inks. This holds a teeny bit more ink, but overall irrelevant.

This does work, but i recommend the con50, which is being discontinued, so buy

title: fantastic everyday blue
text:
Blue velvet is a superb ink. It's very smooth, lubricate nibs fabulously. A modest red sheen, heavy saturation, good manners on all papers, a tiny bit water resistant, with very little shading. this Ink is a deep, saturated true blue and really does smooth out a scratcher nib.

Overall I am quite happy with this, it really distinguishes itself from other inks. The closest I can think to this would be the Goulet exclusive noodles liberty's Elysium, which doesn't sheen, isn't qui

title: Good ink, just not really for everyday use.
text:
A really minty green, more of an irish green than anything else, but paired with the silver pearlescent shimmer, it's a pretty darn cool effect, particularly in broad, stub, or flex nibs. It can be a little hard to read in dry nibs smaller than a M, so bear that in mind.

A fun ink to write letters

text:
Oxblood is a fantastic ink. The swatch doesn't do it justice. It really does go down a dark, gothic maroon comic-book blood color. Noodlers Antiem is a REAL dried blood coppery red, but this is just a gorgeous maroon, pomegranate red with violet undertones instead of any orange or yellow, which makes it much more appealing to read.

It's a well behaved ink, with very little feathering or bleed on cheap paper, and good shading on good paper, medium-wet flow.

title: Easily one of the best writing instruments of all time.
text:
Purchased from Goulet Pens as a gift set, though it is cheaper here.

This is an incredible pen and a piece of history. Bauhaus design from 1966, made for over 50 years now, this is an absolute icon of fountain pens.

title: Lavender purple is a wonderful color!
text:
I bought a bottle of lavender purple as my first bottle of mont blanc ink and am immensely happy with it. It shades heavily, has a small amount of gold sheen, writes smoothly, dries reasonably quickly, has a ton of personality, and is no less than the color of blueberry pie filling (to steal the quote from Matt of the Pen Habit)

The ink does fall down on copy paper, where it does have pronounced feathering, bleed, and showthrough on a fairly dry fine waterman hemisphere, but on good p

text:
This is a fascinating little pen. It's all metal, feels quite sturdy. The nib is a little scratchy but easily smoothed and is bizzarely soft and flexible, ALMOST exactly like a platinum soft fine, you can spread the tines from a western F to about a B with really minimal pressure.

text:

It's smooth, even flowing, and well behaved. I do think it should cost about $8, but for a basic broad nib, it's no frills, no problems. It is exceptionally smooth, almost too smooth for me, but most people would think this is perfect.

text: Not a pen for a first time buyer (get a pilot metropolitan or pilot penmanship) but it's actually a nice writer like most jinhaos. Mine has a hairline crack in the barrel near the bottom, but it's tiny and not really noticeable, so I don't care much. Converter works well enough, jinhao typical nib (it's a little closer to a western F) smooth enough, no real problems. It writes a bit dry, but not so much that it skips or hard starts at all, and can be left for days without drying out.

title: Blue/black is HORRIBLE.
text:

The color is good, and shading is solid, there's actually

text:
I make the case that the noodlers ahab is the best fountain pen for the money there is. It's interesting in design, reliable and effective, and by far the most versatile pen that has ever been made.

THIS IS NOT A FIRST FOUNTAIN PEN FOR THE NEWCOMER. This is a pen for someone who already has one pen and wants something they are willing to fiddle with a bit to tune to their liking. But this pen is DESIGNED to be tuned to the user's liking.

I do think the Konrad and the Ahab are better pens, but if you like thin and small and still want a piston filling demonstrator pen with a flexible nib, this is where the money's at.

text:

text:
I've got enough black inks. Heart of darkness (bulletproof), black quink(old faithful), X feather, and a bunch of greys to round it out. I always wanted to try dark matter, mostly out of novelty. But I quickly realized that it's just a great black ink.

I'm not the biggest fan of blacks, but the novelty of this made me buy it, and I'm glad I did.

text:
Well made, holds more ink than any other converter, and it's got the novelty of a button filler, along with the vacuum seal working as an agitator.

Cleaning these is a pain UNLESS you buy a needle and syringe and blunt thr needle on some fine sandpaper (or if you are lazy, goulet ink syringes)

Simply remove the converter, fill a syringe wiyh water, stick the needle into the converter and flush it out in 20 seconds.

title: As good as it gets for everyday use
text:
What more needs saying other than "i with there was a side spiralbound version"?

Dot grids are lovely, the paper loves fountain pens and can easily handle double sided writing, the covers are durable, and the quality control is oitstanding.

If you use fountain pens to take notes in class, you need rhodia.

title: Great green for your collection
text:
Beautiful blueish green ink with lots of shading and a mild sheen around the edges giving the lettering an almost black comic-book outline on good paper.

Modest feathering on bad paper. Good dry times, no smudging. Good flow.

For the price, this is an outstanding ink.

text:
A more yellowish forest green. Not quite as good as diamine sherwood green. feathering is medium on bad paper (zero on good paper), shading is nice, inkflow is great. The bottle is a good shape for filling pens, and the value is solid.

No sheen.

For the price, this is a great green ink. But I personally prefer diamine sherwood green for this type of color, it's a little deeper and more forest-ey.

title: Superb. Huge, well balanced, super smooth
text:
Great pen. If you want a huge mont blanc pen but are unsure of the size, get a 159 and try it first. The grip section is enormous, but somehow is really comfortable.

Jinhao has really stepped up the game on quality control. This nib is glassy smooth, a medium (it says broad in the listing but it's just a typical western medium) and the converter works great. text:

text:
Firstly, if you're looking for a first bottle of 1670 to try, there's no contest that Emerald of Chivor is the most amazing ink in the collection. I'd rank this one third, behind rouge hematite, but this one is still an outstanding buy.

A great grey ink on its own, enhanced by some beautiful gold sparkle. There's some good shading going on in the grey, and with a really wet, broad nib, some really serious gold flake going on.

Bleeding and feathering are extremely minimal, a

title: Don't even think about not buying this. BUY IT.
text: This is one of the most insane inks in existence. Pictures do NO justice for this, trust me, it's got color variation that no camera can pick up. title: All noodlers inks are fantastic.
text: I'm not 100% on Dragons Napalm Red, it's a little more orange-red than red with very limited shading. But it's still typically fantastic noodler's quality, glass bottle, feeds brilliantly, and is PH balanced, so it'll just get used less often than my other noodlers inks.

text: Nice shading and unique color. A little light for office use. Behaves well in my pens.

title: Cool ink by any standard!
text: I really like this stuff. No clogging or other horrors people claim about IG inks. It shades like crazy. Yes it gets darker as it sits awhile. A bit of a dry ink. Way cool.

title: Blackest Ink
text: I'm really into black inks. I've used them all and thought Aurora black was as good as it got until HOD. This is really super black ink.  It smears black, not grey, blue, or red as others. Incredibly saturated ink, yet flows fine. It's a good value on a ton of ink too. The free pen smells bad and leaks if it's not full of ink (the instructions notify you of this). In short, I recommend because it is the blackest ink I have ever seen (and I'm an ink nut).

title: Smooth as glass...
text: Of course the Elite is an interesting pen. The slide cap is satisfying, the inlaid nib is a visual focus, and the balance is great. The real feature is the nib. Perhaps I got an extra smooth one, but it really is like glass. Almost zero resistance or feedback. Smoother than my sailor pro-gear slim, smoother than my lamy 2000, and smoother than my vanishing point. I got the medium and it's kinda nuts.

title: Holds ink.

Here's the only thing, buy it direct from diamine and it's like two or three bucks plus nine shipping. So order a dozen of your favorite diamine inks and it's less than half the price offered here.

title: Great pen.

title: Been using for more than a decade.
text:
I'm a fountain pen guy. I own dozens, including some higher end gold nib piston fillers. The Hero 266 is wet, smooth, and reliable. Ten packs are available on that auction site for 14 dollars. Some are duds, so get the ten pack and find your dream pen.

Oh, they last too. I bought my first pack in 2009 so I've been using a Hero 266 for more than a decade.

title: Very interesting, thin ink.

title: Well constructed and writes very well
text: I had a Waterman ballpoint from Staples for maybe 20 years and lost it. I loved the refills. I didn't really like the aesthetics of that old pen even though it was somewhat expensive. This one costs way less, looks and feels better, and gets me back in the Waterman ballpoint game.

The pen itself is excellently made. The click is not noisy, but clearly positive. I am completely happy with this pen.

title: Rites great. Somewhat purplish or darkish red.

Probably this red color is more legible, which, after all, is the name of the game for Rite in the Rain. And it writes without any issues at all, leaving a rich, clear line.

I have a number of blues (Oxford, Serenity, Salix, Regency, Horizon, etc.)  This is definitely lighter than those. It's elegant through simplicity.

text: At first glance this looks pretty good. The chrome looks shiny. The click is nice. You can get free promotional pens with Chinese refills. At least it writes. Checked the bottom of the box and yes, the whole thing comes from China. I think I'll leave this junk on a counter somewhere for some needy person.

title: Excellent Notebook Glare-Free Paper

title: Beautiful Ink

title: The perfect blue refill
text: The perfect shade of blue and the perfect width for me. I wish Fisher sold pens with this refill. I find their medium way too broad.

title: Writes well, nice color
text: Some brands of non blue/black/red ink write poorly. This lives up to the Fisher standard: smooth writing, no globbing. The color is fairly light (if it were darker, then it would probably be a poorer counterpoint to blue), but usable.

title: Poor printing mars an otherwise OK notepad

I didn't expect it to be as solid and substantial as my OA, but it is. Very nice piece of engineering. The cap fits on perfectly too. I liked it so much, I bought another for myself (the nitride version).

title: Beautiful pen and of course writes well too

I'm not going to go into all of the reasons for that but this is what you'd pay for it if you were standing in a shop in Japan spending US Dollars that had been exchanged for local currency. This isn't coming directly from Pilot, at least mine didn't. It comes from a pen shop in Japan.

title: This is the Platinum proprietary converter you need for Platinum pens
text:
Platinum pens use a proprietary converter. This is that converter. You can get ridiculously deep discounts on Platinum #3776 Century* pens on Amazon, a $200 pen for $70 or so ... but they don't come with converters. If you're going to use bottled ink then this is the converter for those and other Platinum pens.

*That's what I did; $67 for the pen, $9 for the converter and a $200 pen is in my pen case for $76.

The paper is heavy but lacks real "tooth" which is fine for me since I mostly use fountain pens and various inks with some ink wash. The cover material is a bit weird and seems to absorb moisture but not necessarily bad.

I bought the CON-40 converter and it works great with the pen but has a fairly small ink capacity. They tend to dry out quickly in my pens and usually bleeds or feathers on all but the "higher end" papers like Rhodia. It's a nice purple color that I wish was a little darker toward black with a finer drier nib it's just to purple for me.

title: I love this ink
text: I really like the Scabiosa ink. It is a wonderful color that dries fairly quick with some water resistance. Not much bleeding or feathering on a variety of papers. I am going to try one of their other colors in the iron/nut gall. I am not noticing any issues drying out in my pens. But I am going to heed the warnings and flush with water at every refill.

This is a truly EF nib and writes pretty well with the fude bent nib. Fine for a pocket pen that you would only use occasionally. Don't expect this to be a cheap Kaweco Lilliput because it is not.

title: Nice dense black ink

I am still on the fence if this is my favorite black ink because I think Diamine Jet Black performs better on ALL types of paper. The Herbin can be more troublesome on cheaper papers.

Once I run out I either buy ink refills or buy another set, but these will last you a while though gel pens always do have a tendency to run out quite fast. Probably because you'll end up using them so much! Ordered a set for my friend who apparently gave them to her mom for Christmas. That's what being family's all about for the holidays, alright.

text:
Quink has been around forever and I use it in my old pens with rubber bladders - no problem. It is made, I think, in the same factory as Watermans. The only difference I detect is Quink is a purer blue, and Watermans Serenity Blue (? was called Florida Blue) has a slight touch of turquoise. title: Too small to fit
text:
Something is very wrong. The standard clip that I've used for years measures 13.9 mm across the flats. It slides onto a Kaweco Sport easily and stays in place. The paper weight is light, so there is some light ghosting on the reverse side. It performs pretty much like Egyptian bagasse paper or Brazilian eucalyptus paper. A good buy.

title: This blue-black is much closer to black
text:
This is a good, well-behaving ink at a good price. But as far as color goes, it is too close to pure black for my taste.
I would try their plain blue ink, though.
Here is a hint for those who like blue-blacks. Buy a pure blue ink and a small bottle of brown ink (I like Pelikan Brilliant Brown). Experiment with mixtures, maybe 90% blue as a starter. The results are very nice.

title: A great free flowing ink
text:
This is an extremely neutral blue. No hints of black, no hints of turquoise, no hints of green, and color saturation is medium. I did not expect this from Diamine, whose colors tend to be complex and quite brightly saturated. It is just what I wanted and works perfectly in my dry-writing Sailor.

There could be only 2 downsides 1) some may find the color neutrality to be boring; 2) the free flowing characteristic may result in ink blobs with older pens or pens that are already "wet noo

title: More blue than black
text:
This ink has medium flow and medium color saturation. So it is pretty much a middle of the road ink, just like Watermans. If you are a fan of blue-black inks, this might be too close to a pure blue for your taste. It is hardly distinguishable from Diamine Presidential Blue, which is about the purest, most neutral blue there is. I plan to add some drops of black ink to bring it into the more traditional hue of blue-blacks.

I love the clean, simple bottle - worth it just for that.

title: Every day carry
text: A well built and very practical tool. I carry it everywhere. Didn't know how much I needed this until I bought it. 4 stars because the chrome finish is slippery to hold. A dull black model would be better.

title: Small capacity

The cover is thin and not too many pages so that it opens flat and is great for travel. No bleeding even with strong inks in free flowing pens. I'm buying more.

title: I was curious. Now I’m a Curidas fan.
text: The Platinum Curidas joins the brotherhood of “retractable-pens”.  Mont Blanc, Stipula, Pilot Vanishing Point, and the Lamy Dialog 3 are all in the rank and file. The Curidas is a nice addition with a smaller price tag. I like that the Curidas is not a hooded nib like the  Vanishing  Point. It has a modern look with a cool design when the nib is deployed. The medium nib writes well laying down enough ink to make a fountain pen addict satisfied. Highly recommended.

title: Tiny bottles, essentially an expensive sampler.
text:

Probably should be less expensive based on how little ink you get.

title: My shrink said,” slow down on the inks.”
text:
I have many beautiful inks. My psychiatrist has told me to slow my roll, but I can’t.
Iroshizuku, Waterman, Mont Blanc, Diamine,Pelikan,
Noodlers and Parker Quink. I grew up with Parker and Sheaffer ink.
The truth is that Parker is a great ink at a great price. Get some and write something profound.

title: Candy Apple Red, it’s pretty but don’t drink it, it’s ink.
text:

I filled my Montegrappa Otto Zebra with this beauty and wrote on Tomoe River paper.
Vibrant red! My other red is Iroshizuku momiji. The Pilot red is a less serious but a very nice color.
Same company two different reds.

title: Lovely ink
text: This is a really superior writing ink. I was surprised to find that the hue actually was what the title said, 'old golden green' (which the the supplier should have translated, as not many Americans know German). It reminds me of some gilded ornamental object with a patina, or perhaps green olives glistening in the sunset. It flows like magic (from a Parker IM) but it does show significant feathering on low-quality papers.

title: One of my workhorse inks.
text: Easily the easiest cleaning ink I've ever seen- even on cloth this stuff comes readily out with cold water and blotting with a wet paper towel. Smooth, basic bright blue, suitable for an office setting or for personal writing. Works well in every pen I have from a very wet Pelikan m205 to a very dry Pilot Metropolitan.

text: I love writing with fountain pens. A buddy recommended this color to me and I had to get some. Glad I did, because the color is indeed very well balanced. The green is like fresh mowed grass, but it's dark enough to be used every day. I've tried it in a few pens and so far no issues. Happy with it!

title: Excellent Mechanical Pencil!
text: I wanted this pencil for quite some time, and I finally got the gumption to buy it. I'm glad I did. It is an overbuilt pencil that I see lasting for several decades. I got mine in 0.7mm and the color blue is beautiful.  Sometimes I do forget it's a pencil and not a pen! I get compliments on it all the time too.

title: Got this for my Schneider Ray Rollerball!
text: Works well in my Schneider Ray Rollerball pen. Filled it up and stuck it in the pen and it works perfectly.

title: Excellent Green/Black Ink!
text:
I tried a sampler of this ink, and I loved it. So I had to buy more. I've run it in a couple pens, and no issues. The black is unique. On some papers it shows up as a green/black (mostly black), but it's got a great color quality about it. It's different than the usual blue/blacks out there.

I've also tried it in the Schneider Ray roller ball pen (takes fountain pen ink). Worked well in that too!

title: Works Well in Staedtler 925 Pencils!
text: I got this for some 2B leads for my Staedtler 925 mechanical lead holders. Works well. They seem a little darker for 2B, but I'll take it for the price. Works well for sketching.

title: A BEAST of a Pencil!
text: I have a few of these pencils. I use them with all different grades and colors of leads. The lead tube is brass, and there is NO plastic to break. Very dependable and long lasting pencils. I've never had one break.

title: Works well in the Staedtler 925 20 Series Pencils!
text:
I got these for doing sketching without using wooden pencils! It saves space, allowing me to carry a full gamut of colors in my pocket.

It's a bit of a hassle to swap out colors, but it makes you think before changing colors a bit.

They can also be sharpened by your normal lead pointer. I use the OHTO brass sharpener.

title: Excellent for the Pentel Orenz 0.3mm Pencil!
text: I got these to refill my Pentel Orenz sleeved mechanical pencil. I love these leads. They are spot on with the lead hardness, and they resist breakage. Very happy with them!

title: Fude Fountain Pen Nibs are Awesome!
text:
I had to get this pack for some of my fountain pens. They are Jowo #6 (for use in x450/x750 and more). I've used them in other pens that take Jowo #6 nibs and feeds.

I do a lot of drawing, and having a fude helps do neat stuff.

For the price, you can't go wrong. Takes 30 seconds to swap nibs.

title: Very Nice Pencil!
text: I had to get one because of the price. I'm very satisfied with the 0.3mm lead. It's just the right size for sketching and even general writing. Also there is more availability of replacement leads versus 0.2mm and for like half the price. I ordered some Pentel Ain Stein in different grades to see what I like. It looks like the Orenz comes with HB lead from Pentel from the factory. Very happy with the pen. The clutch is brass too. It's a precision machine that's for sure!

title: More of a magenta then a "red"! Looks nice though!
text:
Typical Waterman ink. Safe for any pen.

This red is more or less magenta on most paper. If you want a true red or a "darker" red, like an oxblood, I would suggest adding some Waterman Intense black ink to it or even blue to it, or both. Like do a cut of 50% red, 25% black, and 25% blue. Haven't tried it yet, but I'm sure it'll darken it up a bit.

The ink flow is medium in most pens -- not too wet and not too dry. It seems to dry very quickly.

Overall it's a nice

title: Similar to DC Supershow!
text: This ink is very similar to Montverde DC Supershow. It's a rather dark blue, and has some shimmer to it, depending on the type of paper. The flow is a medium, and has a medium-fast dry time. Overall it's a nice color ink.

title: Erases Perfectly!
text: I've always like these erasers. Especially for sketching and even just general use. The 4 pack should last me the rest of my life. They erase even the darkest of graphite with ease.

title: Nice Color!
text: I've always like Sheaffer's blue ink. Been using Sheaffer pens since grade school. It works great in any pen. Has a nice color and sheen to it. Very happy with the ink!

title: Excellent Sharpener!
text: I got this for sharpening my Staedtler 2.0mm pencil. It works great! It also keeps the graphite shavings contained. Very happy with it.

title: Excellent for testing inks!
text: I get a lot of sampler inks to see their color. Instead of loading them into a regular fountain pen, I use this to test the inks out to see if I like them. Also handy if I only need a certain color for a very short time. Say for drawing. I really like it!

title: Comparing it to other inks...
text:
Comparing this to Noodler's ink is not close. I was expecting it to similar to Noodler's, and was I surprised.

I'm not sure what Noodler's puts in their black ink, along with some of their darker inks, but whatever it is, it leaves black deposits in the feed and under the nib that require more cleaning than necessary. It's almost like black soot. Maybe it's carbon particulate? Not sure. It actually clogged up my Parker Jotter to the point it wouldn't write. When I took it apart, I was

title: Excellent Blue Ink!
text:
I'm on a blue spree, and I've been trying all different brands of blue ink. This one ranks right up there as a quality everyday ink. I'm happy with it's dry time and it's color. It's a good blue color, comparable to most blue ball points.

Flow is good in a Jinhao x450 with a Goulet Pens Medium nib.

title: Amazing Ink!
text: This ink writes very well. It makes a couple of my rough writers, write much nicer. The ink flow is right on par, and there is minimal feathering even on the worst paper. It also dries quick as well. I got the same ink, but in blue that I ordered. Can't wait to try that color out. Very, very pleased with this ink.

title: Nice Looking Ink!
text:
It's color is similar to Pelikan 4001, but it's a bit wetter, and it has a medium flow rate.

Works in all my fountain pens, and it dries quickly.

I'm happy with it.

title: Nice Color, but a bit dry!
text:
I wanted to try this ink to see how it worked. It has a nice color, and the bottle looks neat. However, it just seems to be a dry ink. If you have a wet fountain pen, this ink will dry it up.

Since it's a drier ink, it does dry fast. So for folks that are lefties, it will dry before you hand gets to it.

Overall its an OK ink. Would I buy more? Likely not. I might try the Edelstein inks next after I go through this.

title: It writes!
text: Does what it's supposed to do - write. Ink flow and feeling is just like the original.

title: Excellent Spiral Notebook for Heavy Duty Use AND for Fountain Pen Users!
text:
I've been hunting for either a A4 or Letter (or equivalent) sized ruled notebook mainly for fountain pen use. I've been using Five Star 1 subject notebooks for a while, but their quality has been slowly going downhill. Every other page, the toothing is in the opposite direction, or the fibers are different. Very annoying. One sheet could be good, and the next 3 might be horrible.

In any event, I prefer Rhodia, the paper is nice, but the notebook construction is less than desirable. Al

title: Works well! Easily Cleaned!
text:
I got this for my Platinum Plaisir, and it works well. You can fully disassemble this converter. As far as I know, this is the only converter you can fully disassemble to re-grease it with silicone. I've run a few different types of inks through it, and no staining, and no issues. Very happy with it.

Only gripe is that it's a tad pricey.

title: Great Fountain Pen!
text: Comparing this to the JinHao 750x, TWSBI Eco, and the Pilot Metropolitan series, it's something in-between. The nib is smooth and small, but the whole pen is small. Great for small hands or if you need a non-obtrusive looking pen. I bought the Parker Deluxe Twist converter for it. text: I can't believe how smooth this pen writes. The feed is right on the money too -- not too dry and not too wet! I filled it with Noodler's Air Corp Blue Black Ink, and it writes amazing! Extremely happy with it. In comparison to my other fountain pens (TWSBI ECO, VAC700R, and JINHAO X750), it writes smoother than all of them. title: Wow! Amazing Pen!
text:
I cannot believe how well this pen writes and works! It is on par with my TWSBI and Pentels. I am very pleased with how smoothly it writes. I am running Noodlers Zhivago Ink in it. The feed works perfect, no leaks, no excess - just the right amount of flow. I am extremely pleased with this fountain pen. The barrel is solid and has a chunky feed. It holds well in my hand. Looking forward to many good years of use of this pen.

title: Works in Lamy Al-Star!
text: Works well in the Lamy Al-Star. As a helpful hint, I highly recommend dipping past the nib to get a complete fill without air bubbles. I used Noodler's EEL ink in my Lamy. The converter works well, the Lamy Al-Star, eh, it will likely be my kicker pen.

title: Does not fit Flattop (School Pen) V3!
text: I was hoping that I could use a converted with my old 90's School Pen Flat Top. No dice. The metal band makes it just a hair too thick to fit into the barrel. Will likely return it, because I don't have any other Sheaffer pens.

title: Nice Looking Pen, but Nib and Feed Needs Attention
text: I've been using fountain pens since I was a kid, and I got a small collection of them. Been wanting an inexpensive Lamy to add to my collection. Out of them all, this one ranks mediocre. I like the look and the feel, but the nib is just, blah. I don't know if it will just take time to break in, or if I need to adjust it. The nib just seems way too scratchy for a medium. text: I'm kind of a pen and pencil fanatic. I bought this one to add to my collection. Very nice pencil. I do plan on using it though. I mostly write and draw with them.

title: Works Well in a TWSBI VAC700R! Very Deep Black Color!

text: I'm a 0.9mm pencil fanatic, and I had to add one of these to my collection. For those that are wondering, yes it's got a plastic clutch. While I'm not all that crazy on plastic clutched pencils, for the money, I wouldn't expect it to be brass.

title: Great Inexpensive Pencil!!
text: I mostly write with pencil, due to ease of corrections and the fact that it you can use it for all conditions and materials. Since I use 0.9mm a lot, I purchased the P209. Works well and is nice and light. Seems super durable as well.

title: Very Good Pencil!
text: I got this as a backup to my GraphGear 1000, and I've go to say, it is a very nice pencil. Feels nice to click, and the knurled handle is nice to grab. Overall a great pencil.

title: Excellent Writing Utensil!
text: I've had this pencil for a couple weeks now and I keep it with me everywhere I go. I like the fact that the lead is nearly unbreakable and the fact that one piece of lead goes on, and on, and on.... and on! Only downside is the fact that not everywhere has the 0.9mm lead. title: Modernized Writing Utensil!
text: This is one interesting pencil! I bought it after doing some research on mechanical pencils. I've used it a lot, and I like the fact that it turns the lead as you write keeping the lead sharpened as a conical point resulting in precise writing. It will not rotate if you are simply doing gradient filling, because of the way the mechanism works. But for regular drawing and writing, this pencil is the latest technology in writing utensils. Very cool!

title: Wonderful ink for a lefty
text:
I am left-handed and tend to have sweaty palms. I've been using this ink for the past three months and it's perfect. It has a wonderful gray-blue color that darkens to a soft blue-black as it dries. The ink's color changes noticeably depending on how much is laid on the page, giving your pen strokes a cool shaded look. Best of all, it's extremely waterproof and does not smear—even with my hands, which is impressive. I'm using it in a Sailor 1911 Full Size. It's absolutely wonderful.

title: Vibrant color and writes dry.
text: The ink did help me get a wet writing pen to write a bit drier. It is a good color but does stain the converter. I will not put it in one of my transparent pens as the staining would be obvious.

title: Good permanent ink
text: packaging and delivery were great. I bought this ink to make a wet writing fountain pen write drier but unfortunately it wasn't the answer. The ink itself is just fine, the color change is very nice and its permanence would be great for important documents. I did not have any problems with it gumming up the filler mechanism. I think it is good to have in my collection of ink but again my notion of reducing the wetness of the nib did not work.

title: It's PERFECT!
text: Just the right size and the paper is wonderful. I have always had success with Rhodia papers and books. It was delivered promptly and well packed. Can't wait to fill it up!

title: Great Brown!
text: Very hard to find a brown body pen but this one is just perfect, The fine point is very smooth and the ink flows perfectly. Love this pen.

title: Smooth writer!
text: I am so pleased with this pen. The medium nib tends towards the fine side which I like and is very smooth. Wile this is a smaller size fountain pen it is very comfortable for me, light weight and easy to carry. The color is unusual and looks like a much more expensive pen.

title: Great black ink
text: This is a very rich and dark black, in fact, it is my "go to" black. Worth every penny and flows well.

title: Great Red Ink
text: What a beautiful ink this is - just wish the particles would stay suspended longer but still a great addition to my ink collection. It is truly the color of blood but the flecks in it make you think less of blood and more of shimmer.

title: Well crafted pencil
text: These pencils hold their point and are beautifully made. The only downside that I can see is that awful bar code label which does not come off - it takes away from the sleek look and finish of the pencil. It would be 5 stars without the bar code!

title: Beautiful Ballet Pink Ink
text:
This ink is a lovely soft, gentle, ballet pink. I like it best in my Noodler's Ahab with a 1.5 Goulet Italic nib that I purchased from Goulet Pens.
The ink arrived on time and in perfect condition.

title: So smooth!
text: Received these as a gift from a dear friend, and I am delighted. They lay down beautiful, smooth lines. Highly recommended.

title: Excellent for fountain pen ink
text: I bought this journal to experiment how it would handle fountain pen ink. I've used nearly every ink and nib I own, and couldn't be happier. The lined paper is smooth and sturdy. The binding has held up to daily use for the past couple of months, as has the elastic band. I find the size very comfortable. I will definitely be ordering more of these.

title: Love this pen
text: I received this as a gift from a dear friend who shares my fondness for fountain pens. I have a Lamy Safari that I enjoy very much. This model is everything I love about that pen made even better. The nib was super smooth and crisp straight out of the box. The aluminum body feels comfortably light, yet pleasantly substantial. It's a very comfortable writer. Highly recommend.

title: Beautiful ink
text: I tried a sample of this ink over the summer, and liked it so much that I placed it on my wish list. The color is dark purple, and if you use a flex nib you'll see some lovely shading. I wanted this ink to test in a pen that likes to ooze ink from the feed (despite heat setting, trying different nibs, etc), and I was very happy with the results. No oozing, and it's easy to clean out the pen. Given the fact that this is an iron gall ink, I'd recommend that you clean your pen regularly.

title: Super popular - and with good reason

title: Excellet pen, well worth the price.
text: I'm really enjoying this pen. I worried that it might feel too large/cumbersome to write with, but my worries were for nothing. It's comfortable, well-made, and worked without any of the tuning or fussing that fountain pens sometimes require. It inks and cleans easily, and has shown no problems with drying up or stuttering even after I've left it unused (stored point up in a pen cup) for over a week. If you enjoy fountain pens, you'll likely love this one.

title: Great value, very smooth writing.

I accidentally murdered my old fountain pen by using calligraphic ink -- which is why I had to buy a new one. No amount of cleaning will get that stuff out of a fountain pen. I'm enjoying this pen so much that I may end up getting another one.

title: Nice basic teal
text:
this is a nice teal, with good flow characteristics. The small bottle is economical and came well-packed.

I'm only giving four stars because I've been spoiled by some teals that really make this one look dull — Iroshizuku Syo-ro and Sailor Yama-dori.

The Diamine does clean out of the pen quite nicely though, and I'm not worried about using it in an older pen.

title: Very long pencil. Also, eraser is adjustable — you can slide it up as you wear it down!
text:
I purchased these to see what all the fuss is about. Sure they're more expensive than something like a Dixon Ticonderoga, but they're actually cheaper than many drawing pencils and other high-end quality Japanese brand pencils. (These actually are made in Japan.)

The 602 pencils have a glossy, lacquered graphite-colored painted finish (not black.) The Cedar is dense and smooth and doesn't crumble much, even with a dull pencil sharpener blade. The (graphite) lead is perfectly centered.

title: nice ballpoint pen refill, but consider the parker gel refill instead
text:
I thought these would be something better than their typical ballpoint pen refills, since Quink is the name of their water-based fountain pen ink. But no, this is just a nice oil-based ballpoint pen refill.

If you want bold flowy ink for longer and nicer writing, instead get [[ASIN:B001AFB6YI Parker Refill for Retractable Gel Ink Pens, Medium, Black Ink, 2 per Pack (30525PP)]] in the same sized cartridge. Ballpoint pens really aren't that great for writing letters.

title: good replacement refill if you're tired of your Parker pen refill bleeding all over your pants.
text:
Not really a good refill for writing a letter or novel, but it's not meant to be. Ballpoint pens in general, because of their high-viscosity oil-based ink, require some pressure to write, and thus don't write super smoothly.

However, they do write on everything, and are good for miscellaneous notes and labels and are good to keep in a pocket or glovebox.

These work perfect in Parker Jotter pens (they come with an adapter)

the tip doesn't really roll as smoothly as an expensive pen, but it's pretty good for a $1 gel pen.

title: not completely consistent, but reliable, smooth, and bold

I don't think the quality is *quite* consistent in these pens though — the black pen felt slightly scratchier across the page than either the blue or purple pens, but at this price I think perhaps I can live with that.

That was a *huge* problem with my prior notebook brand. I'll happily take ghosting over ink bleeding any day.

Always a pleasure to write with. Perfect for the fledgling fountain pen enthusiast, for those with repetitive stress injuries who write a lot (these pens need only a light hand), and for those who want decent pens for a fair price. Another plus: not many people know how to write with these properly, so if someone asks to borrow a pen and you hand over one of these, you're likely to get it back. ;)

For that reason I use it, on better quality paper, in lower cost pens, and produce script that uncommonly pops off the page.
